name: Event with Prof. Martin A. Sinozich (Finance) + Date Factory Tour
description:
A learning day combining a finance-focused session with Prof. Martin A. Sinozich, Senior Lecturer in the Entrepreneurial Management Unit at Harvard Business School, followed by a visit to a Date Factory.

Martin teaches Finance to CEOs and Managing Partners who own and operate family-owned firms, large and small, as part of HBS's Executive Education Owner/President Management Program. Before joining the HBS faculty, he worked in large financial institutions including Fidelity Investments, MBNA America Bank, and Prudential Home Mortgage, where he led innovation teams adopting new technologies into the corporate DNA, including developing some of the earliest internet capabilities at MBNA America Bank in 1995-96 and the first remote workforce capabilities at Fidelity Investments in 1998-99. 

A practical, owner-operator lens on finance, especially relevant for members running family businesses, paired with a hands-on, sensory experience at the Date Factory to round out the day.

name: AI for busy spouses - Spouse only event
description:
AI as Your Personal Operating System: Family Brain + Work Brain

This will be a practical, hands-on session designed for spouses who want to understand how AI can become a useful thought partner in both family life and work/business life — not just a tool for answering questions.

The session will focus on how to use AI to create more clarity, reduce mental load, and build simple personal systems across two areas:

1/ Family Brain  
How AI can help manage the invisible work of home and family life — planning, decision-making, schedules, calendars,, activities, household admin, and staying organized.

2/ Work Brain  
How AI can support business owners, professionals, and community leaders with thinking, writing, planning, research, decision-making, and follow-through.

What we’ll cover:  
•⁠  ⁠How to give AI better context so it understands your life, priorities, family, and work  
•⁠  ⁠How to create reusable systems instead of starting from scratch each time  
•⁠  ⁠Practical examples of AI helping with family planning, home admin, work planning, communication, and idea development  
•⁠  ⁠⁠An example of how to automate tasks like inbox triage and scheduling family calendars 
•⁠  ⁠A guided co-working section where participants can start building their own “family brain” or “work brain” live in the session  

What participants will walk away with:  
•⁠  ⁠A clearer understanding of how to use AI beyond basic prompts  
•⁠  ⁠Practical templates they can reuse immediately  
•⁠  ⁠A simple starting structure for their own personal AI system  
•⁠  ⁠Confidence using AI as a thought partner for everyday family and work decisions  

The tone will be practical, accessible, and hands-on

description:
A regional cricket tournament bringing chapters together on the field. Each participating chapter fields a team of 11 members, competing in a T10 format with proper scoring, umpiring, and tournament structure, much like a professional league.
The tournament runs over two days at the Sobha Stadium, with a dedicated event theme tying together the matches, presentation, and overall experience. A few celebrity appearances are also being planned to add to the buzz around the event.
A high-energy, competitive format designed to bring out chapter pride and camaraderie in a completely different setting from the usual learning and social events.

name: Global Academic Exchange – with Prof. Niro Sivanathan & Prof. Florin Vasvari
description:
Global Academic Exchange — with Prof. Niro Sivanathan & Prof. Florin Vasvari
A two-day executive learning experience bringing together two of London Business School's most respected faculty for a chapter-exclusive engagement.

Day 1 — Negotiation, led by Prof. Niro Sivanathan, Professor of Organizational Behavior at London Business School, renowned for his expertise in influence, negotiation, and decision-making. He has worked extensively with YPO Global and chapters, with his events nominated for or winning YPO "Best of the Best" awards, and regularly advises and coaches YPO members on negotiations related to exits, acquisitions, and other strategic deals ranging from $35M to $2B. 

Day 2 — Private Equity, led by Prof. Florin Vasvari, Executive Dean of Executive Education (Middle East) and Academic Director of the Institute of Entrepreneurship and Private Capital at London Business School. He teaches Distressed Investing and Private Equity and Venture Capital at the school, combining academic rigor with practical industry expertise. 

The two days close together with a one-hour collaborative session bringing both professors on stage, exploring where negotiation and private equity intersect, a fitting close given that the two have already co-designed and co-direct LBS's own Private Equity Negotiations Programme together.
resource: Prof. Niro Sivanathan & Prof. Florin Vasvari

An intimate, closed-door session drawing on decades of real boardroom experience in building brands and leading through high-stakes moments.

name: Strategic Leadership Intensive – 1 Day Program with Prof. Das
description:
A full-day executive leadership program led by Prof. Das Narayandas, the Edsel Bryant Ford Professor of Business Administration at Harvard Business School, who returns to the chapter following his earlier masterclass. He has been an HBS faculty member since 1994 and has won the Robert F. Greenhill Award for Outstanding Service to the HBS Community, the Charles M. Williams Award for Excellence in Teaching, and the Apgar Award for Innovation in Teaching. 

His scholarship focuses on market-facing issues in business-to-business marketing and professional services, including client management strategy, delivering service excellence, and channel design. He has consulted and developed in-house training programs for companies including GE, IBM, J&J, Honeywell, Mitsubishi, Tata Group, and Microsoft, among others. He currently sits on the board of Titan Company Limited. 

A day designed for senior leaders looking to sharpen strategic thinking and client/customer management frameworks at the highest level, backed by decades of real-world consulting and classroom expertise.

A dignified, memorable experience designed to celebrate a community that rarely gets a night like this, while showcasing the chapter's leadership in giving back.

name: Global Affairs & Leadership Forum – with Prof. Hise Gibson
description:
A 4-hour executive learning forum with Prof. Hise Gibson, Senior Lecturer in the Technology and Operations Management Unit at Harvard Business School, and a retired Colonel with 25 years of distinguished service in the United States Army. His research focuses on operational effectiveness, leadership, leader development, human capital development, change management, and leading teams through crisis. He has received the Legion of Merit and Bronze Star for his military service. 

Built around two 80-90 minute case study sessions, with a 30-minute break between each, totaling 180 minutes plus breaks. Per the call with Prof. Gibson on 17 June 2026, the sessions will anchor on:

Crisis leadership and organisational change — practical, actionable approaches leaders can apply directly, not just theory
Scaling through three lenses — people, process, and technology, examined as the core levers for organisational scale

A high-intensity, case-driven format designed to leave members with concrete frameworks they can apply immediately, not just inspiration.

name: Jeffersonian Dinner & Deal Talk – Curated Executive Dialogue

It opens with the Deal Talk, a closed-room exchange limited to 15-20 people, designed for candid, off-the-record conversation on real deals, decisions, and lessons learned. This is followed by the Jeffersonian Dinner, bringing the full group together around one shared conversation, classic Jeffersonian style, rather than scattered table talk.
A high-trust evening built for genuine connection, intimacy, and unfiltered exchange rather than panel-style Q&A. Speaker to be confirmed.
